newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Top Milosevic associate backs election concessions.
newsitem.headline: Top Milosevic associate backs election concessions.

text.p: One of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's most powerful associates has endorsed an OSCE report calling for recognition of opposition victories in municipal elections, state media said on Tuesday.

The disclosure that Dragan Tomic, speaker of the Serbian parliament, favoured concessions signalled a possible end to a marathon political crisis in which police had started attacking and beating pro-democracy demonstrators.

Tanjug, the official Yugoslav news agency, said Tomic spoke out on the volatile issue during a meeting on Tuesday with a delegation of West European Social Democrats dealing with three straight months of street unrest in Serbia.

"Tomic said the Serbian leadership backed an (investigative) report submitted by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE) ... He said a solution to the (election) issue must be found through legal means, saying efforts were being made to resolve the issue as soon as possible," Tanjug reported.
Serbia's authoritarian ruling Socialists had previously admitted only four of 14 defeats in election in major municipalities across the country later annulled over alleged "irregularities".

Ljuba Tadic, organiser of a protest rally in Belgrade on Tuesday, said he had learned via unofficial channels that Milosevic had instructed his prime minister to abide by an OSCE recommendation to reinstate opposition election victories.
